# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by tools/docs.py from the code. Don't edit it by hand. -->

Every command of `wm` 0.5.0. Read commands take `--json`; their payloads are described in the [JSON schema reference](json.md).

Exit codes: `0` success; `1` refused, or problems found; `2` usage error.

## Environment

- `NO_COLOR`: set to any value, even empty, and the text output carries no color. It wins over `FORCE_COLOR`.
- `FORCE_COLOR`: set to any value but empty or `0`, and the text output carries color even when it isn't going to a terminal.
- `TERM=dumb`: no color on a terminal.
- JSON output never carries color.
- On a terminal, prose in `wm show`, `wm inbox`, `wm check` and `wm doctor` wraps to the terminal's width, from 60 to 100 columns. Output that isn't going to a terminal is never wrapped.
- When the output's encoding can't show the glyphs, they're drawn in ASCII.

## wm init

Create the record, or set up this machine in a clone that has one.

```
wm init [--atlas NAME] [--tool NAME] [--yes]
```

- `--atlas`: make this repository an atlas: a record that several code repos share
- `--tool`: an agent tool to set up; repeatable (default: claude-code)
- `--yes`: ask nothing, even on a terminal: a project with every agent tool, and no CI

## wm update

Regenerate the files Waymark owns, and add any missing record folders.

```
wm update
```

## wm doctor

Check wm, git and this project's setup; changes nothing.

```
wm doctor [--json]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version

## wm ci

Add a GitHub Actions workflow that installs the pinned wm and runs wm check.

```
wm ci
```

## wm pr

Describe a pull request from a change: its title and description.

```
wm pr [--json] <change> [--repo NAME]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version
- `change`: the change's name
- `--repo`: in an atlas, the code repo it is for

## wm atlas

Register atlases on this machine, point code repos at them, check their setup.

```
wm atlas <command>
```

## wm atlas register

Register this atlas on this machine, with its code repos found through their path hints, or one code repo at a folder.

```
wm atlas register [repo] [folder]
```

- `repo`: a code repo's name, from the atlas's settings
- `folder`: that code repo's folder

## wm atlas point

Write the pointer file that tells this code repo which atlas holds its record.

```
wm atlas point <atlas> [--path FOLDER]
```

- `atlas`: the atlas's name
- `--path`: the atlas's folder, relative to this repository's top

## wm atlas doctor

Check this atlas's registry entries, code repos, branches and pins; changes nothing.

```
wm atlas doctor [--json]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version

## wm hook

Answer an agent tool's hook event, read as JSON from standard input.

```
wm hook <tool> <event>
```

- `tool`: the agent tool whose hook this is
- `event`: the tool's name for the event

## wm new

Create a change, milestone, exploration or resource from the built-in template.

```
wm new <change|milestone|exploration|resource> <name> [resource-kind] [--short] [--owner NAME] [--milestone MILESTONE] [--after CHANGE] [--from EXPLORATION] [--by NAME]
```

- `kind`: one of `change`, `milestone`, `exploration`, `resource`
- `name`: a kebab-case name, for example add-search-limit
- `resource_kind`: for a resource only: service, platform, account, database, dataset or document
- `--short`: put a change on the short path
- `--owner`: a change's owner (default: your git name)
- `--milestone`: the milestone a change belongs to; links it from the milestone's roadmap
- `--after`: the change this one comes after; its unmerged branch is this one's base
- `--from`: the exploration a change or milestone comes from; its status then leads to it
- `--by`: who the (proposed) record in a change's milestone names as its writer (default: "planner for <your git name>")

## wm accept

Accept a change, so its items can be applied. For the human to run.

```
wm accept <change> [--by NAME]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm tick

Tick an item: it has been applied.

```
wm tick <change> <item> [--by NAME]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm block

Record that an item is blocked.

```
wm block <change> <item> <reason> [--by NAME]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2
- `reason`: why it is blocked
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm gap

Record a spec gap: the record wasn't enough to build an item.

```
wm gap <change> <item> <note> [--by NAME]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2
- `note`: what is missing from the record
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm note

Write a note about an item still to be finished, such as a partial result, in the change's Log.

```
wm note <change> <item> <text> [--by NAME]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2
- `text`: the note
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm revise

Record why an accepted change was edited, before the human accepts it again.

```
wm revise <change> <why> [--parts PARTS] [--by NAME]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `why`: what the edit changed, and why
- `--parts`: the parts it changed, separated by commas: item numbers, "proposal", "design" or "specs/<area>"
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm review

Record a self-review of a change, once every item is ticked.

```
wm review <change> --self SUMMARY [--finding FINDING] [--by NAME]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `--self`: what the review checked and found (required)
- `--finding`: a finding, written <critical|warning|suggestion>: <place>: <text>; repeatable
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm verdict

Record a reviewer's verdict on a change.

```
wm verdict <change> <pass|changes|spec-gap> <reasons> [--items ITEM] [--finding FINDING] [--by NAME]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `verdict`: one of `pass`, `changes`, `spec-gap`
- `reasons`: the reviewer's reasons
- `--items`: the items to rebuild; a "changes" verdict names at least one
- `--finding`: a finding, written <critical|warning|suggestion>: <place>: <text>; repeatable
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm reopen

Reopen an item that a review of its change named to rebuild.

```
wm reopen <change> <item> [--by NAME]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm resolve

Record what was decided about an item or a change's review that went to the human, and free it.

```
wm resolve <change> <item> <decision> [--by NAME]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, or "review" for the change's review
- `decision`: what was decided
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm sync

Merge an applied change's deltas into the specs without archiving it.

```
wm sync <change> [--by NAME]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm archive

Archive an applied change, once the human says yes.

```
wm archive <change> [--built TEXT] [--differs TEXT] [--override REASON] [--by NAME]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `--built`: what was built, for the outcome
- `--differs`: how it differs from the proposal; none when left out
- `--override`: archive although review records are missing; the reason is recorded
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm close

Close a milestone whose changes are all archived.

```
wm close <milestone>
```

- `milestone`: the milestone's name

## wm roadmap

Change a milestone's roadmap: add, drop or move a change's line, with a record.

```
wm roadmap <command>
```

## wm roadmap add

Add a planned line for a change at the end of a milestone's roadmap.

```
wm roadmap add <milestone> <change> <description> [--by NAME]
```

- `milestone`: the milestone's name
- `change`: the change's name, for example add-search-limit
- `description`: what the change delivers toward the goal
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm roadmap drop

Take a change's line off a milestone's roadmap, with the reason.

```
wm roadmap drop <milestone> <change> --reason REASON [--by NAME]
```

- `milestone`: the milestone's name
- `change`: the change's name
- `--reason`: why the change is dropped (required)
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm roadmap move

Move a change's line on a milestone's roadmap.

```
wm roadmap move <milestone> <change> [--after CHANGE] [--first] [--by NAME]
```

- `milestone`: the milestone's name
- `change`: the change's name
- `--after`: put it right after this change's line
- `--first`: put it at the top of the roadmap
- `--by`: who the record names as its writer (default: your git name for your own acts, "planner for <your git name>" for what the planner writes)

## wm exploration

End an exploration that won't be acted on: drop it, with the reason.

```
wm exploration <command>
```

## wm exploration drop

Drop an open exploration with the reason, and move it to the archive.

```
wm exploration drop <exploration> --reason REASON
```

- `exploration`: the exploration's name
- `--reason`: why it won't be acted on (required)

## wm status

Show where things stand: changes, milestones, what needs you.

```
wm status [--json]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version

## wm inbox

Show what only the human can resolve.

```
wm inbox [--json]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version

## wm show

Show everything about one change, spec, milestone or exploration.

```
wm show [--json] <name> [--kind KIND] [--from ATLAS]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version
- `name`: its name; an archived change or exploration also by its dated name
- `--kind`: which kind, if the name is shared; one of `change`, `spec`, `milestone`, `exploration`, `resource`
- `--from`: read a spec from an atlas this project references

## wm ls

List changes, specs, milestones or explorations.

```
wm ls [--json] <changes|specs|milestones|explorations|resources> [--archived] [--from ATLAS]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version
- `kind`: one of `changes`, `specs`, `milestones`, `explorations`, `resources`
- `--archived`: include archived changes, milestones or explorations
- `--from`: list the specs of an atlas this project references

## wm instructions

Say what to do at a step of a change: the file, its template, the rules, the commands.

```
wm instructions [--json] [explore|propose|specs|design|tasks|apply|review|archive] [--change NAME]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version
- `step`: the step (default: the change's next step); one of `explore`, `propose`, `specs`, `design`, `tasks`, `apply`, `review`, `archive`
- `--change`: the change (default: the only one)

## wm context

Print the context pack for exploring, implementing one item, or reviewing one change.

```
wm context [--json] [change] [item] --for ROLE
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version
- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2; none for a review
- `--for`: the job the pack is for; one of `explore`, `implement`, `review` (required)

## wm check

Check the record's health: format, links, conflicts, evidence.

```
wm check [--json] [--fix]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version
- `--fix`: first rewrite the record in its standard layout; wording is never changed
